- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Bill blunder - Environmental levy bill withdrawn, replaced after certification cock-up.
Debate on a bill titled ‘The Environmental Levy Act 2026’ had to be suspended on Friday in the Senate and the proposed statute withdrawn and replaced as the document that was first before the Upper House was not a money bill. This cock-up triggered a stern warning from acting leader of opposition business, Professor Floyd Morris, who described the error as unfortunate. Lengthy presentations were made on the bill and the senators had taken lunch break to resume deliberations.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: It’s been an intense hurricane season in the Pacific.
Tropical storms have spawned in the Pacific in what seems like assembly-line fashion in recent weeks, as El Niño conditions that emerged in June have caused waters to grow warmer than normal, setting off a chain of unusual weather around much of the world. “It’s ramping up to be perhaps the strongest El Niño on record,” University of Miami hurricane expert Brian McNoldy said.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Why AI has trouble predicting hurricane intensity.
THE CONVERSATION: Artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionised weather forecasting in just a few years, with global AI weather models now able to produce forecasts that rival some of the world’s best physics-based prediction systems. This remarkable progress has been driven by three factors: massive amounts of weather data, advances in AI models, and unprecedented computational power. While most of the current discussion on improving AI for weather focuses on the models or new hardware, the data is crucial.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: ‘He was too great to stop at his death’ - JP Samuels Youth Foundation keeps legacy alive.
For Alex Ward, losing his best friend Jean-Pierre ‘JP’ Samuels felt like losing a brother and a purpose at the same time. Samuels died on September 29, 2025 with so much still ahead of him. The 25-year-old had just finished his master’s degree in corporate finance and was about to start working at a wealth management firm so he could support his mother when he suddenly took ill and died shortly after. But instead of letting his name fade, Ward and a group of Samuels’ closest friends turned their grief into action and launched the JP Samuels Youth Foundation.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that any attempt by India to divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”. “Any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the waters will be treated as an act of war. India must make no mistake about it,” he said during a speech at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, where he called attention to the neighbouring country’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Six big takeaways from a turbulent week of UN diplomacy.
Limousines whisked world leaders away from the United Nations on Friday after a week of speeches, meetings and hallway diplomacy. While they reached no breakthroughs on the world’s most intractable conflicts, talks on the Iran and Ukraine wars inched forward and global powers used the venue to debate AI risks with industry leaders.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Iran proposes Hormuz plan, Trump reportedly refuses.
Iran offered a plan to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz, Tehran said on Friday, but within hours, reports indicated that US President Donald Trump rejected the proposal. The waterway, key to the world’s oil supply, is central to the conflict between the United States and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months. But new mediation efforts at the UN’s gathering of world leaders in New York this week offered some optimism of progress toward a deal.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 'Largest hypocrisy in the world': Pakistan tells UNGA India’s 'terrorist exports' have gone global.
Pakistan on Saturday accused India of having “elevated propaganda into statecraft”, embraced disinformation as diplomacy and “exported terrorism as an instrument of policy”, as Islamabad hit back at remarks made by the Indian representative at the UN General Assembly.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Russia targets Ukraine's digital nerve centres as war reaches data infrastructure.
Recent Russian assaults have targeted Ukraine's data centres and telecommunications, severely diminishing internet access for numerous households. A Datagroup facility was among those impacted, leading to tragic casualties and extensive damage. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy emphasized that these strikes threaten vital services essential for daily life. Russia defends its actions by alleging that these sites were linked to military intelligence, highlighting how modern warfare increasingly relies on digital infrastructure.

The Central Intelligence Agency has alerted European countries, including Spain, France, and Italy, about a looming threat involving Russian drones potentially launched from commercial ships. These drones may be hidden within shipping containers and aimed at key infrastructures like airports and ports. While the intent is to cause disruption rather than large-scale damage, it heightens the necessity for vigilant monitoring of airspace and civilian maritime activities across the Mediterranean.
